mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2.5% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances with UNRATE < 3.5%, or UNRATE < 3.5% does not correlate with increased corporate earnings over the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with broader economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline does not correlate with reduced corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals robust consumer demand and a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and labor market
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint movement of RSAFS and UNRATE does not correlate with positive market returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in low-growth environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition of high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not correlate with negative market returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a single month signals strong job growth, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 months signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with broader economic slowdown indicators.
